changes.headline: The synthetic verdict scored at +$5.70 on a traded settle; December WCS widened on volume
changes.dek: New from Friday's ICE file (Oct 23): TMS Dec26 +$5.70 on 300 lots, first traded settle since Oct 13, below both verdict lines (+$7.00, +$6.50). TMW Dec26 -$28.50 (was -$27.85), down $0.65 on 555 lots; WCS Dec outright $74.77. ARV Dec26 -$20.00; ARV to TMW spread +$8.50 unchanged.. Friday's ICE settlement file landed after Saturday's edition. Dec26 synthetic crude settled at +$5.70 on 300 lots (ICE TMS settle, Oct 23), the contract's first traded settle since Oct 13 (+$4.55 on 40 lots), below both pre-registered return lines of +$7.00 and +$6.50, so the return verdict grades on the supply-return side: when December synthetic actually traded, it traded under the scarcity lines. The same file shows WCS Dec26 widening to -$28.50, down $0.65 on 555 lots, reversing Thursday's traded tightening on the strongest flat-price session of the episode, with WCS Houston Dec26 at -$20.00 and the ARV to TMW December spread unchanged at +$8.50. C5 Dec26 settled at +$5.25 on 90 lots and MSW Dec26 at -$1.95. The tape grades a price, not a plant: no public return confirmation exists for the autumn turnaround windows, and third-quarter volumes (Imperial and Cenovus on Oct 30, Suncor on Nov 3, Vermilion on Nov 4, MEG Energy on Nov 5) remain the arbiters.
changes.balance_read: Synthetic returning and heavy widening on the same traded day is the basin's split in one file: the upgrader leg is pricing normalization while the heavy front leaks against flat-price strength into November apportionment of 19 percent lights and 7 percent heavies. The verdict is a price grade; volumes can still overrule it within the week.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD settles, Oct 23, 2026 (Friday file, landed after the Oct 24 edition); Q3 calendar as confirmed Oct 20 to 24

changes.headline: The diesel crack closed below $100; Saturday's Saudi ledger is a fourth day of interceptions and claims
changes.dek: Diesel crack $97.78 on completed Oct 23 closes (was carried at $105.66 off the pre-close refresh); 3-2-1 $51.34. The sustained run above $100 that began Aug 17 has ended. Saturday: one confirmed interception toward Khamis Mushait (fourth straight day); a Houthi claim against the air base itself, unconfirmed; the seven-vessel claim at day four with no corroboration.. On the validated crack history refreshed this edition, Friday's diesel crack closed at $97.78 and the 3-2-1 at $51.34, on a heating-oil settle that was essentially flat against a $3.80 crude rally. The diesel crack is below $100 for the first time since the sustained run began on Aug 17; the series counts 42 total closes above $100 and its maximum stands at $117.92 (Sep 16). Saturday's confirmed event, via the Saudi Press Agency, is the coalition intercepting an explosive-laden drone toward Khamis Mushait, a fourth straight day of confirmed interceptions; the Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile salvo at the air base at Khamis Mushait itself, with no damage assessment or Saudi statement published. Friday's Abha airport and Jazan refining claims remain unconfirmed. The Revolutionary Guards' seven-vessel claim has produced no advisory, no named vessel and no independent report in four days, against the Central Command position that the mine claims are incorrect.
changes.balance_read: The crack led this complex for two months and has now lagged two sessions running; a distillate crack sliding back toward double digits removes the premium bid under synthetic barrels at the same moment the synthetic tape prints below its scarcity lines. The confirmed barrel impact of the week's Saudi campaign remains zero; the premium is compounding on claims and tempo, not on lost supply.
changes.publishers: Validated crack history refreshed Oct 25, 2026; Saudi Press Agency via Arab News, Oct 24; Reuters, Oct 23 (Friday claims; Central Command denial of Oct 22)

changes.headline: Ukraine claimed a second strike on Ryazan; DOE pages unchanged into a stacked week
changes.dek: New: Ukrainian General Staff claims of overnight Oct 23 to 24 strikes on Ryazan (about 342 kb/d) and Novoshakhtinsk (about 100 kb/d), unverified. Unchanged: DOE awards for both reserve rounds still unpublished; posted contracts 133.56 Mbbl to 13 companies; Lake Charles cause still undisclosed. Ahead: Northeast heating oil bids Tue Oct 27; Q3 season opens Fri Oct 30; OPEC+ Nov 1 to 2, most likely Nov 2.. Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck the Ryazan refinery and the Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov region overnight Oct 23 to 24, reporting fires at both (via S&P Global, Oct 24). The claims were not independently verified and no Russian damage assessment had been published. Ryazan's main primary unit has been halted since the Oct 15 attack and trade sources said the plant had recently resumed crude intake, so a second strike on the same address extends the Russian product-supply subtraction the diesel waiver programme is meant to offset; Slovakia's prime minister said Friday there is no official deal on that programme and no exports yet (Reuters, Oct 23). The Department of Energy's pages are unchanged: no award for the Sep 29 round or the Oct 16 re-offer whose proposals were due Oct 21, posted contracts at 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies, and no stated cause for Friday's emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels to a Louisiana refinery.
changes.balance_read: The Russian leg is tightening on claims while the waiver leg thins on politics; neither is a confirmed barrel yet. The week's confirmed events are all dated and calendar-shaped: a bid deadline, an earnings season that grades the synthetic verdict, and a producer meeting carried into the highest settles of the episode.
changes.publishers: Ukrainian General Staff via S&P Global Commodity Insights, Oct 24, 2026; Reuters, Oct 23; DOE pages checked directly Oct 25; OilPrice, Oct 24 (OPEC+ meeting most likely Nov 2)

flags.title: Hormuz flows above pre-war on exports; the seven-vessel claim is silent for a fourth day
flags.detail: Kpler puts Middle East crude exports at 17.3 Mb/d in October, above the 16.9 pre-war average, with Hormuz flows at 11.7 Mb/d, about 82 percent of pre-war (Oct 22). A trade-press loadings count puts Hormuz loadings at 12.64 Mb/d over Oct 1 to 21, about 9 percent below the pre-war daily average (Oct 24); loadings and transits are different measures and neither shows a flow collapse. The Revolutionary Guards' claim of seven vessels hit or mined has no named vessel and no independent corroboration after four days, and US Central Command called the mine claims incorrect. In Saudi Arabia, the coalition has confirmed interceptions four days running (Oct 21 to 24), the national oil company evacuated its Dhahran headquarters on Thursday with no operations disruption reported, and Saturday brought an unconfirmed Houthi claim against the air base at Khamis Mushait after Friday's unconfirmed claims against Abha airport and the Jazan refining complex. Trade the flow prints and confirmed incidents, not the claims. Trigger: Independent corroboration of any claimed incident, a named vessel, a flow print stepping down, a Saudi statement of facility damage, or an operations impact from the Dhahran evacuation

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: first US cargo at sea; no official deal per Bratislava; November tranche is the supply test
flags.detail: The first tanker under the waiver loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading for New York, arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, shipping data). No signed supply contracts have been confirmed and no further loading has been reported. Slovakia's prime minister said after meeting Putin on Oct 23 that there is no official deal on Russian diesel exports to the United States and no exports yet (Reuters). The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The binding constraint is Russian refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit is halted since Oct 15, the plant was claimed struck again overnight Oct 23 to 24, and the largest refiner is stretching repairs from days into months. The import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027 and the waiver has no fixed expiry. Trigger: A first loading for the November tranche, a named US buyer or signed-contract confirmation, a Ryazan restart report, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights; December call unregistered; the synthetic verdict is scored
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). December's nowcast opens at persistence on those levels and no December judgment call is registered yet. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST, and on the published pattern (October's notice Sep 16, November's Oct 20) the December notice is expected around Nov 19 to 20, after nominations close, so the call must be registered as a judgment call rather than read off the notice. WCS Dec26 settled at -$28.50 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 23) on 555 lots, widening on traded volume, and the synthetic return verdict scored the same day at +$5.70 on 300 lots, below both registered lines. Trigger: Registration of a December judgment call before Nov 17, third-quarter volumes on Oct 30 and Nov 3 grading the synthetic tape verdict, or a second traded front-month move on Monday's settlement file

flags.title: Freight fixtures are correcting; the Baltic Week 43 weekly has still not published
flags.detail: Spot fixtures have eased for a second week: a VLCC on Arabian Gulf to China fixed at $29.61 million (Oct 22) against a Gulf to China cost print near a record $37.37 per barrel earlier in the week, Brazil to China at $48 million, and US Gulf to China near $60 million against a $79.6 million October record. Spot earnings colour (Oct 23) holds near record highs on a round-voyage basis that is not comparable to the weekly prints. The Baltic Exchange Week 43 weekly had still not published as of this edition, a full week stale; the last confirmed weekly is Week 42 (Oct 16), TD3C WS 1281.25 (TCE $1,370,193 per day) and TD9 WS 830. At prevailing Caribbean to Gulf levels, freight still forces competing heavy sellers toward deeper FOB offers into the Gulf and pressures WCS Houston; easing at the margin reduces the incremental pressure, it does not shelter Canadian barrels. Trigger: Publication of the Baltic Week 43 weekly, a verified fixture materially below the $29.61 million print, or a TD9 print confirming the correction has reached the Caribbean to Gulf leg

forward_calendar.what: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results
forward_calendar.detail: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them. The synthetic return verdict, now scored on the tape at +$5.70, is graded against these volumes.

forward_calendar.what: OPEC+ meeting (Nov 1 to 2, most likely Nov 2)
forward_calendar.detail: Five analysts surveyed by Reuters (Oct 23) expect another modest December increase; delegates said after the Oct 5 meeting that the November increase was the last before a first-quarter pause. The spread between those two is the meeting's actual risk, carried into the highest settles of the episode.
Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data.
Vermilion reports the quarter on Nov 4 (announced Oct 21). A smaller read on the basin than the majors, carried for calendar completeness.
MEG reports Q3 on Nov 5 (earnings call Nov 6), confirmed from the company's events calendar on Oct 24. A thermal producer read on the quarter.
Deliveries under the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels) are to complete by this date.

December's Mainline nowcast opens at naive persistence on November's print (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert). No December judgment call is registered yet. Nominations close at 0700 MST.
